title: midstream-fragment-anchoring-and-delimiter-coalescing
author: Maya Kline
description:
Motivation: We continue to see customer-reported flakes where SSE streaming produces truncated or malformed JSON fragments when delimiters ("

" or event sentinel lines) arrive split across TCP/HTTP chunks or when backpressure reorders in-flight write windows. This manifests as partial JSON objects, duplicated delimiters, and non-deterministic ordering of function-call sentinels for tool invocation. This PR introduces an anchoring and coalescing layer in the stream adapter to make mid-stream fragment boundaries deterministic and safe for OpenAI-compatible consumers. Design summary: 1) Introduce a lightweight fragment anchor token ("<<ANCHOR:hexnonce>>") emitted at the start of multi-part events when detection heuristics expect boundary splits. The anchor is treated as meta and stripped before higher-level parsing, but used to reorder/coalesce fragments deterministically on reassembly. 2) Add a delimiter coalescer that normalizes repeated newline delimiters and converts sticky delimiter sequences into a canonical "

" sequence before attempting JSON reconstruction. 3) Add a lease-based event window for function-call sentinels: tool-call boundaries get a transient lease ID so that fragments that arrive slightly out-of-order can be re-sequenced within a short symmetric window rather than being dropped or misattributed. 4) Implement checksum-guided fragment anchoring: the adapter computes a 16-bit rolling checksum over the last N bytes of a fragment to detect mid-fragment corruption after reassembly and retries on failure. Compatibility and safety: All modifications are opt-in behind the new feature flag REDWOOD_STREAM_ANCHORS=false by default for non-breaking rollouts. For OpenAI-compat mode the flag defaults to true because OpenAI-style clients are more sensitive to partial JSON. Test strategy: unit tests added for parser reassembly, integration harness that simulates chunk boundary permutations and backpressure reorder scenarios, and a new chaos test in perf-canary that replays customer-captured packet traces (anonymized). Migration and rollout: feature-flagged staged rollout (20% -> 60% -> 100%) with observability hooks that surface fragment-rescue counts and anchor-lease collisions. If the rescued/failed ratio degrades latency SLAs we will rollback to previous flag configuration and investigate. Checklist: - [x] Parser code and adapter changes implemented - [x] Unit tests for fragment reassembly - [x] Integration tests simulating boundary permutations - [x] Perf canary chaos replay added - [x] Docs updated describing anchor semantics - [x] Feature flag gating and metrics emission - [x] Manual review and QA on internal streaming client harness
commits: add: stream anchor token and initial coalescer (parser+adapter)
fix: normalize delimiter sequences and canonicalize SSE preamble
feat: lease-based event window for function-call sentinel ordering
test: add unit/integration tests for fragmented-chunk reassembly
chore: feature flag gating and metrics for anchor/coalescer
docs: streaming adapter anchor semantics and rollout plan
review_comments: Jonah Patel: Nice approach, I like the checksum guard. A couple of concerns: what's the perf impact on p95 when computing the rolling checksum for very large sequences? Can we keep the checksum window bounded?

Maya Kline: Jonah, checksum window is capped at 8KB and we only compute on fragments that cross the chunk boundary heuristics path. Microbenchmarks added to the PR description. Expected p95 impact < 0.4ms on a T4-equivalent slot.
Elena Ruiz: Lease-based reordering looks promising but we need a deterministic tie-breaker when two leases overlap for adjacent events. Suggest using sequence epoch + anchor nonce to break ties.
Maya Kline: Good call, I've added deterministic tie-breaker: epoch counter first, then anchor nonce lexicographic order. Documented in streaming_anchors.md.
Priya Narang: Tests fail intermittently on CI due to timing assumptions in the chaos replay harness. Can we make retries deterministic or add a small backoff jitter in tests?
Maya Kline: Adjusted the chaos harness to use deterministic pseudo-random seeds for chunk timings in tests and added a short backoff to reduce flakiness. Rerun CI.
CI: Integration tests passed on re-run. All checks green.
release_notes: Stabilize streaming reassembly by introducing fragment anchors, delimiter coalescing, and lease-based ordering for function-call sentinels. Opt-in behind REDWOOD_STREAM_ANCHORS flag (enabled in OpenAI-compat mode). Improves robustness against partial-JSON emits and chunk-boundary delimiter bugs.
